title: Set-Aside Accounts — Charges Paid, Payees and Payment Lead Times by Plan
content:
Each plan of Set-Aside Accounts at Cedarline pays a fixed set of property charges. The tables below are the plan settings that decide which charges a plan pays, to whom it pays them, how far ahead of the due date the servicer pays, who bears the cost of a late payment, how a shortfall is funded and whether payments continue while the loan is due and payable.

## Charges paid and payee

| Plan | Property tax | Hazard insurance | Flood insurance | Homeowners-association dues, ground rent, special assessments | Pays the payee directly | Each tax installment paid separately |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Fully Funded LESA (Mandatory) | Yes | Yes | Yes | No | Yes | Yes |
| Fully Funded LESA (Borrower-Elected) | Yes | Yes | Yes | No | Yes | Yes |
| Partially Funded LESA | No | No | No | No | No (paid to the borrower) | No |
| Repair Set-Aside | No | No | No | No | Yes (to the contractor) | No |
| Servicing Fee Set-Aside | No | No | No | No | No | No |
| Summit Tax and Insurance Reserve | Yes | Yes | Yes | No | Yes | Yes |

"Pays the payee directly" means disbursements go to the taxing authority, insurer or contractor rather than to the borrower. "Each tax installment paid separately" means each installment of a property tax bill is paid as its own disbursement on its own due schedule rather than prepaying the full year.

## Lead times, late-payment cost, shortfall and due-and-payable loans

| Plan | Tax paid at least this many calendar days before the tax bill's delinquency date | Premium paid at least this many calendar days before the premium due date | Bears a penalty or lapse cost caused by late payment | Funding of the unpaid remainder when the balance is short | Payments continue while the loan is due and payable |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Fully Funded LESA (Mandatory) | 15 | 30 | The servicer | Borrower billed, then corporate advance | Yes |
| Fully Funded LESA (Borrower-Elected) | 15 | 30 | The servicer | Borrower billed, then corporate advance | Yes |
| Partially Funded LESA | 0 | 0 | The borrower | Not applicable | No |
| Repair Set-Aside | 0 | 0 | Not applicable | Not applicable | No |
| Servicing Fee Set-Aside | 0 | 0 | Not applicable | Not applicable | Yes |
| Summit Tax and Insurance Reserve | 15 | 30 | The servicer | Corporate advance | Yes |

A lead time of 0 appears where the plan pays no tax or no insurance.

## Reading the schedule

- **No plan pays homeowners-association dues, ground rent or special assessments.** Those charges stay with the borrower under every plan.
- **"Borrower billed, then corporate advance"**: the borrower is billed for the unpaid remainder of a payable charge first; the corporate advance follows only if the borrower has not paid it by the bill's due date. **"Corporate advance"**: Cedarline advances the remainder at once.
- **Same charges, different plans.** The two Fully Funded LESA plans and the Summit Tax and Insurance Reserve pay the same three charges directly to the payee; they differ in how a shortfall is funded.
- **Hypothetical reading.** For an illustrative tax installment with a delinquency date of the 30th of a month, a plan with a 15-day lead pays it no later than the 15th of that month.
